figcaption: Gallery consignment keeps title with the maker; the showroom split pays for editing, rent, and the talk that teaches a buyer to trust the wall.

commons_file: Wendell castle, tavolino da caffè, rochester NY 1967.jpg
alt: Wendell Castle studio furniture coffee table photographed in Rochester, New York, 1967
figcaption: When a table becomes a gallery object, the buyer must decide whether to eat on it or admire it — studio furniture lives in that tension.

commons_file: Shaker ladder chairs.jpg

commons_file: Craft fair 130504-N-WF272-063.jpg

commons_file: A history of oak furniture (1920) (14777817264).jpg
alt: 1920 oak furniture catalog plate showing how listings and illustrated ads presented casegoods to buyers

commons_file: Warehouse interior showcasing organized shelving and packages.jpg

commons_file: Showplace, High Point Market, North Carolina.jpg

commons_file: Shelves stocked with boxes and carts in a spacious warehouse environment during daylight hours.jpg

commons_file: Made in USA label 01.jpg

commons_file: EFTA00002265 - Cluttered warehouse with stacked boxes a fan and shelves filled with supplies under industrial lighting.jpg

commons_file: De Groot showroom, Rushcutters Bay.jpg
alt: Historic De Groot furniture showroom interior, a quiet room after the platform contract ends
figcaption: Walking away from a portal contract often means rebuilding showroom relationships the gallery door once held open.

commons_file: Price list and barbers' purchasing guide of barbers' chairs, furniture, and barbers' supplies (1884) (14781776084).jpg

commons_file: Made in USA label 02.jpg
alt: Made in USA label on consumer goods, a retail claim tied to sourcing and showroom language
figcaption: American made meant traceable labor and domestic supply chains before the word became a filter checkbox.
